messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] r self help: the future...
messages.body_plain:
I agree with meeting every two weeks for the beginners.

The bellow following lecture for advanced meeting is exactly what I need for my research - we will make acoustic recordings of bee family sounds and analyze the data. Unfortunatelly I am a beginner at R. Hopefully I will understand what you talk about...

See you on 14th.

Regards, Dragan

2009/12/18 Maarten de Groot <Maarten...@nib.si>

> Hi R koholiks,
>
> For starters I would suggest to have our first advanced meeting on the
> 14th of January at 16:00h. I invited Dr. Gogala to present the package
> "Seewave". This package gives you the ability to analyze acoustic data.
> As Tomaz already suggested we can after that discuss about the how to
> fill in the workshop for beginners. It would also be nice if some
> beginners would be there to give their opinion.
>
> Just a start for a discussion about the content of the courses and the
> time table ( just to think something over during the holidays;)):
> First there are several options which materials to use for the beginners
> meetings: We could use the lectures of professor Blejec (off course if
> that is alright with prof. Blejec), you can find parts about it on his
> website "http://ablejec.nib.si/R/" or we can use the R book of M.J.
> Crawley (http://www.bio.ic.ac.uk/research/mjcraw/therbook/index.htm). To
> be honest I am not really familiar with prof Blejec his lecture, so I
> can not tell much about it. The R book on the other hand I know more
> about, this gives an introduction to the use of R with contents about
> data input, manipulating dataframes, graphics, tables, mathematics,
> classical tests, statistical modelling, regression, analysis of
> variances, etc etc... Additionally he also provides datasets on his
> website for use. If anyone else has other options please let me know.
> For the advanced meetings it would be nice that everyone presents a
> topic about methods they are working with ranging from simulations,
> multivariate analysis, statistical modeling, genetics analyzes, etc etc.
> I volunteer to gather presentations for the advanced group and schedule
> them for the future meetings. So if you have any idea for a presentation
> please contact me and I will put the dates in an Excel sheet online.
>

> About the time frame: Urša suggested to have twice a month a beginners

>
> meeting and once a month an advanced meeting. I think this is a nice
> idea, as the beginners than can faster learn R and the groups can than
> fuse in a later stage.
> I would therefore suggest the following dates on 16h:
> Beginners course:
> 28-1, 11-2, 25-2, 11-3, 25-3, 8-4, 22-4, etc
> advanced course:
> 14-1,17-2, 17-3, 14-4, 13-5, etc
>
> It would be nice if advanced users could also attend the beginners, so
> they can help the beginners with R problems.
>
> This is a kick off for this discussions, I am looking forward to your
> reply and/or additions to this email.
>
> lp,
>
> Maarten

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Roman,

A cannot help you with gedit because I don’t know what is wrong with your procedure. However, you might try solving your problem from a different perspective. J People find using EMACS with R plug-in quite helpful (see http://www.stat.duke.edu/courses/Spring04/sta244/computing/R-ESS.html or ask google), however, I strongly recommend using Rkward (http://rkward.sourceforge.net/) under linux – I find it to be even nicer than TinnR… Indeed it is meant for KDE desktops but I run it on Ubuntu Gnome withouth any problems. I was quite happy with its hint function and code completition and useful tabs instead of a bunch of windows for every helpfile I opened. I know this is no answer to your question, but it might just help.

Luka

Job Description:
The USGS Upper Midwest Environmental Sciences Center is seeking a
quantitatively savvy ecologist with expertise in one of more of the
following areas: population ecology, community ecology, biogeography,
conservation biology, landscape ecology and wildlife habitat modeling. The
position would entail, after initial instruction, modeling and mapping
patterns in species occupancy and abundance, avian community analyses, and
extinction risk estimation.  The position is structured as a one-year
research associate position, based in La Crosse, Wisconsin, with potential
for extension depending upon availability of funding.  Start date:
February 2010, negotiable.  Pay schedule: GS-9 (~$47,500 annual salary).

Qualifications:
An M.S. in a wildlife discipline with a strong quantitative background.
The ideal candidate will have direct experience with avian ecology, common
avian sampling protocols and a deep understanding of the assumptions
underlying the standard analyses of such data.  Demonstrated excellence in
scientific writing is an essential qualification.  Good oral and written
communications skills in English are required. The project depends on the
ability to work effectively, without day to day supervision from the
Principal Investigator. Pertinent skills include Bayesian statistics and
programming in R and WinBUGS.

messages.subject: IMPORTANT!! Rkoholik beginner's course announcement
messages.body_plain:
PLEASE READ THROUGH THE E-MAIL EVEN IF YOU ARE AN ADVANCED USER, AS WE WILL NEED YOUR HELP!

Dear Rkoholiks,

At the advanced user's meeting on Wednesday, we finalized the details for the previously discussed beginner's course of our favorite software package (R, of course). So, these are the conclusions, and "rules of the game" both for lecturers and participants:

We decided that the curriculum would follow the online book of Andrej Blejec. It has everything that's needed to learn R, is not as scary as the Crawley book, and is freely available on the Internet.

The sessions will be held every two weeks, on Wednesdays, at 16:00.

All lessons will be "hands on", meaning that you will get to work directly through the study material. Each session should last approximately 2 hours. They will be organized into two parts: first, the topic will be explained (but the participants get to work through the explanation on the computers), and second the participants get assignments they try to complete, and get help if/when they run into problems. We're also discussing follow-up homework assignments that would be provided in an e-mail during the week when there are no lessons. In this manner the participants would have a chance to run into their own problems, and solve them at the next session. This homework, however, will depend on the time the person organizing a lesson has available and may not happen after each session.

So, this is the schedule proposed so far:

20. 1. 2010 - Chapter 3: How to start (with R)
4.2.2010 - Chapter 4: Objects and data structures
18.2.2010 - Chapter 4: Objects and data structures
4.3.2010 - Chapter 5: Data import/export

18.3.2010 - Chapter 9: Plotting (graphs)

This schedule will be updated as we go along. There are currently five people ready to prepare lessons: Roman, Maarten, Tomaz, Martin and Prof. Blejec (we wish him a speedy recovery from his accident). Later, in May, Pina and Luka will also be joining the lecturers. We also hope that as many advanced users as possible will be available in each session to help with problems. Also, if anyone else is willing to participate as a lecturer, he or she is VERY VERY WELCOME!

Technically, all meetings will be held in the computer lab (B6) at the Biology Department, Večna pot 111. There is a number of computers available there, but it would be appreciated if you also bring your own laptops if you can. We will provide and open Wi-Fi network at each session so that you can connect to the Internet and with other computers.

Each lecturer will announce his/her lecture a week before the session, and provide the required material (data files etc.) for the people that bring their own laptops to best use the course time (so that we don't run around with USB sticks). The lecturer will also be responsible for the follow-up homework (at his/her discretion).

The first lesson will be prepared by Roman. He'll send the details shortly.

Hope to see you all there next week!

Cheers,

Maarten and Tomaz

messages.subject: R: ciklus predavanj za začetnike - 1) Splošni uvod v R
messages.subject_clean: R: ciklus predavanj za začetnike - 1) Splošni uvod v R
messages.body_plain:
Dragi Rkoholik,

v duhu prejšnjega elektronskega sporočila vse  zainteresirane na tem mestu vabim, da se nam pridružite na predavanju in delavnici o R-u.

Predavanje in delavnica z naslovom "Splošni uvod v R" bosta naslednjo sredo, 20.1.2010, ob 16:00 v računalniški učilnici B6 Oddelka za biologijo (Večna pôt 111). Teme, ki jih bomo pokrili zaobjemajo zagon R-a, delovni prostor ("workspace") in zgodovina, delovni direktorij, namestitev paketov, iskanje pomoči in nekateri  urejevalci kode. Teme bodo povzete po 3. poglavju priročnika "Introduction to R" avtorja Andreje Blejeca, ki si ga lahko na svoje računalnike prenesete z njegove spletne strani <http://ablejec.nib.si/R/> (najdete ga pod poglavjem "Moj priročnik").

Kdor ima prenosni računalnik, je priporočljivo, da ga prinese s seboj.
Za vse tiste, ki vas zanima urejanje kode v ločeni aplikaciji (priporočljivo) vam svetujem, da si namestite enega od programov (seznam ni mišljen kot popoln pregled): Tinn-R <http://www.sciviews.org/Tinn-R/> (priporočen kot prva izbira), Notepad++ <http://sourceforge.net/projects/notepad-plus/> (priporočljiv še dodatek NppToR <http://sourceforge.net/projects/npptor/>), RKWard <http://rkward.sourceforge.net/>. Na srečanju bomo spoznali prednosti pisanja v zunanjih urejevalnikih besedila.

V kolikor se komu utrne vprašanje v zvezi s predavanjem, ali pa namigom kaj bi rad slišal na predavanju, mi to prosim pravočasno sporočite.

Zahtevnost in teme predavanja bodo pisana na kožo slušateljem, ki se z R-jem še niso spoznali ali pa šele stopajo prve korake.

##########################################################

Dear Rcoholics,

as announced in a previous email, I hereby invite everyone:

next Wednesday, 20.1.2010 at 4pm (16:00 for you metrics), will be a lecture entitled "General introduction to R". Lecture will follow 3rd chapter of manual Introduction to R by Andrej Blejec (available at the author's site <http://ablejec.nib.si/R/>).

Personal laptops are welcome. Anyone interested in editing his or her code in external editors, I would advise to install at least, but not limited to, one of the following editors: Tinn-R <http://www.sciviews.org/Tinn-R/> (recommended), Notepad++ <http://sourceforge.net/projects/notepad-plus/> (plugin named NppToR <http://sourceforge.net/projects/npptor/> recommended), RKWard <http://rkward.sourceforge.net/>.

lp(Roman)

messages.subject: Re: ciklus predavanj za začetnike - 1) Splošni uvod v R
messages.subject_clean: ciklus predavanj za začetnike - 1) Splošni uvod v R
messages.body_plain:
Rkoholik, pozdrav!

Za nami je prva delavnica, v kateri smo si pogledali nekaj osnovnih funkcij, ki jih R zna. Povzetek vsebine današnjega predavanja (workshop1_basics.R) in domačo nalogo (workshop1_homework.R) lahko najdete na strani mailing liste (http://groups.google.com/group/rkoholiki/files). V kolikor kdo ne bi uspel dostopati do datotek, naj mi to sporoči.

workshop1_basics.R (http://groups.google.com/group/rkoholiki/web/workshop1_basics.R) na kratko predstavi kar smo se danes pogovarjali na delavnici.

workshop1_homework.R (http://groups.google.com/group/rkoholiki/web/workshop1_homework.R) vsebuje domačo nalogo za vse tiste, ki bi radi povadili kar smo se danes naučili. Vaje sem nekoliko predelal in dopolnil, tako da bodo primeri zanimivi tudi za tiste, ki ste nalogo na delavnici že rešili.

Obe datoteki imata končnico .R, vendar pa jih je mogoče odpreti s katerimkoli urejevalcem besedila (Notepad, Wordpad, Notepad++...). Priporočam, da uporabite kak urejevalec besedila, ki zna obarvati R sintakso in se mogoče tudi pogovarjati z R-om. V Windowsih je najpopularnejši Tinn-R (http://sourceforge.net/projects/tinn-r/). Več o urejevalcih si lahko preberete v workshop1_basics.R. Vrstice, ki imajo v prvi vrsti lojtro (#) so mišljeni kot komentarji. Če vsebino datoteke spustite (npr. copy/paste) skozi R, bo le-te ignoriral.

V kolikor pa ima kdo kako vprašanje, pa le pogumno!

lp,
Roman

messages.subject: plotting time series
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rkoholiki,

I am working at the moment with three time series of temperature. Now I
wanted to use ts.plot(), because with this function you can plot more
time series in one plot. Now I tried it but it does not work. You get
the following warning "Error in .cbind.ts(list(...), .makeNamesTs(...),
dframe = dframe, union = TRUE) :  no time series supplied".

Here is an example (copy and paste into R):

maxtemp <- c(20,24,25,29,21,25)
meantemp <- c(19,22,22,26,19,22)
mintemp <- c(16,19,28,22,15,18)
cbind(maxtemp,meantemp,mintemp)

ts.plot(maxtemp,meantemp,mintemp,lty=c(1:3))

Apparently it does not read my time series. Can someone help with this
problem?

Hvala!

Maarten

messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] plotting time series
messages.body_plain:
The problem is that ts.plot demands a ts class object. Your mean, max and mintemp objects are all vectors. As soon as I find the time, I will see how can POSIX elements be transformed into ts class.

See ?as.ts or ?is.ts and http://www.stat.pitt.edu/stoffer/tsa2/R_time_series_quick_fix.htm

Cheers,
Roman

messages.body_plain:
Something like this <http://groups.google.com/group/rkoholiki/web/marteenplot.jpg>? The plot is in need of tweaking, but I hope the general idea is clear. This was done in ggplot2 and the code to do all the steps is below.

setwd("/spajza1/r/help/maarten/")
library(ggplot2)

t.data <- read.table("lowertemp.txt", header=T, sep="")
t.data <- transform(t.data, date = paste(month, day, sep="-"))[,-c(1:2)] #melt day and month
date <- strptime(as.character(t.data$date), format="%B-%d") #convert date to POSIXct class
t.data <- cbind (t.data[, c(1:3)], date)

dta <- ggplot(t.data, aes(x=date, y=meantemp)) +
    geom_line(linetype="solid") +
    geom_line(aes(y=maxtemp), linetype="dashed") +
    geom_line(aes(y=mintemp), linetype="dotted")

jpeg(filename="marteenqtplot.jpg", width=800, height=600, units="px")
dta
dev.off()

Thanks Roman!

I also found a way how to do it for ts.plot().

maxtemp <- c(20,24,25,29,21,25)
meantemp <- c(19,22,22,26,19,22)

mintemp <- c(16,19,18,22,15,18)
ts.plot(ts(maxtemp),ts(meantemp), ts(mintemp), col=1:2,
main="ts.plot(maxtemp, meantemp, mintemp)", ylab="Temperature")

The catch is that you should put "ts" (time series) in front of the vector.

lp,

Maarten
